question: Does the source-derived matter power disagree with CLASS pk_lin even when both are evaluated at exactly the same native Fourier k nodes at off-native times, while agreeing on common native (k,tau) nodes?
hypothesis: If native-node source-to-Fourier closure remains exact but an off-native-time discrepancy survives at exact native k, the remaining discrepancy is localized to the different time-interpolation operators: CLASS source interpolation of d_m followed by squaring versus CLASS interpolation of stored ln P.

operators.source_path: CLASS get_transfer(z, class format): spline d_m in time, then reconstruct P_source=(2 pi^2/k^3) d_m^2 P_R
operators.fourier_path: CLASS pk_lin(k,z): interpolate stored ln P in time and evaluate at the same native Fourier k node
operators.k_interpolation_control: Only native Fourier k values inside 0.03-0.20 h/Mpc are used for the primary off-native comparison.

classification_rule.pass: All numerical controls pass, native-node closure passes, and the baseline off-native-time source-vs-pk_lin discrepancy survives at exact native k above the preregistered diagnostic floor.

interpretation_policy: A PASS localizes the v0.72-v0.76 source/pk_lin discrepancy to the time-interpolation stage under the frozen linear AeST model, because source and Fourier power agree on common native nodes and differ at off-native times even at exact native k. It does not alter historical FAIL/PASS labels, simulate nonlinear evolution, or constitute observational evidence. After a PASS, the linear numerical-chain debugging is considered closed and subsequent work should move to nonlinear physics using the certified state/native-source representation.
